title: Calendar cubes
prompt: You have two blank dice. Instead of dots, you write single digits on each face. Every morning you arrange the two dice so their front faces show the current day of the month (01–31). You must use both dice, and you can swap their order.
Each die has 6 faces, giving you 12 faces total for the digits 0–9 (plus 11 and 22).
What trick makes it possible to fit all required digits across only 12 faces?
answer: flip 6 upside down to use it as 9
answer_display: Flip 6 upside down to use it as 9
hints: Days 11 and 22 must be possible, so both dice need a 1 and a 2. Days 01–09 require a 0 on each die. That's already 3 digits committed on both dice.
After placing 0, 1, 2 on each die, you have 3 remaining faces per die — 6 faces total — for the digits 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. That's 7 digits for 6 spots.
Which two digits are never needed at the same time?
solution_lede:
The key constraint is that both dice must show a 1 and a 2 (for days 11 and 22) and both must show a 0 (to represent single-digit days as 01–09). That uses 3 faces on each die before you've placed anything else.

You now have 3 remaining faces per die — 6 total — for the digits 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9. That's 7 digits and only 6 slots. The escape: 6 and 9 are never needed at the same time. A 6 rotated 180° becomes a 9. So you only need one face to serve both roles.

Distribute the remaining 6 digits (3, 4, 5, 6/9, 7, 8) across the two dice:
Die one: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
Die two: 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8
(The 6 on die two doubles as 9 when flipped.)

solution_steps.body: Both dice must have 0, 1, and 2 — required for 01–09, 11, and 22. That fills 3 faces each.
Remaining faces: 3 per die, 6 total. Remaining digits: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 — that's 7.
Insight: 6 and 9 are never needed simultaneously. One face can serve as both by rotating 180°.
Final assignment — Die one: 0 1 2 3 4 5. Die two: 0 1 2 6 7 8 (6 doubles as 9).

options: Flip 6 upside down to use it as 9
